topicName: Decentralized Storage: IPFS, Filecoin, and Arweave
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Decentralized Storage: IPFS, Filecoin, and Arweave"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional web architecture relies on centralized cloud providers like AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. In contrast, Web3 relies on decentralized storage networks to ensure censorship resistance, permanence, and cryptographic verifiability. This tutorial explores the three foundational pillars of decentralized storage: IPFS, Filecoin, and Arweave."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Content Addressing with IPFS"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) is a peer-to-peer hypermedia protocol designed to make the web upgradeable, resilient, and open. Unlike HTTP, which uses location-based addressing (where is the file located?), IPFS uses content-based addressing (what is the content of the file?)."},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"Every file added to IPFS is broken down into chunks, hashed using a cryptographic algorithm, and assigned a unique Content Identifier (CID). If a file's content changes even slightly, its CID changes completely, ensuring data integrity."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"# Install IPFS (Kubo) and initialize your local node
ipfs init

# Add a file to IPFS
echo "Hello Web3" > hello.txt
ipfs add hello.txt
# Output will return a CID: bafybeig...abc"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Incentivizing Storage with Filecoin"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"While IPFS is a protocol and network for storing and sharing data, it lacks a built-in incentive layer to ensure files are stored long-term. Enter Filecoin, a decentralized storage marketplace built on top of IPFS."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Storage Providers (miners) offer hard drive space to the network and earn FIL tokens."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Clients pay Storage Providers to store their data over specific epochs (timeframes)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Proof-of-Replication (PoRep) and Proof-of-Spacetime (PoSt) cryptographically guarantee that storage providers are genuinely storing the data they claim to hold."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Permanent Data Storage with Arweave"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Filecoin provides incentivized contractual storage, Arweave focuses on permanent, immutable storage through a novel data structure called the blockweave. Arweave operates on an endowment model: you pay a one-time fee upfront, and the interest generated from this endowment perpetually funds the miners to store the data forever."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Proof of Access (PoA): Miners must prove they have access to a random previous block in order to mine a new block, encouraging them to store rarely accessed historical data."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The Permaweb: A decentralized, permanent web built on top of Arweave where applications and websites cannot be taken down."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary: Choosing the Right Network"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"IPFS: Best for content routing, peer-to-peer file sharing, and temporary caching."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Filecoin: Best for massive, verifiable, enterprise-grade cloud storage contracts with renewal mechanisms."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Arweave: Best for permanent archiving of documents, NFT metadata, and censorship-resistant websites."}]
